categoryEvidence: Fresh 2026-10-27 snapshots: four of eight direct competitors use productivity/tools, two communication, one workflow and one education. Tools matches this extension’s primary translation workflow.
singlePurpose: Translate typed or selected text and, with Pro, eligible webpage text into a chosen language. Related controls provide language detection, optional visible page context, translation tones, local translation history, and restoring original webpage text.

permissions.justification: The popup reads selected text from the current tab’s accessible frames after the user opens the extension, using chrome.tabs.query and chrome.scripting.executeScript in extension/src/ui/main.tsx. This is a real current-tab user gesture flow. Because the package also declares persistent HTTP(S) host permissions for the selection icon, activeTab may be redundant on those sites; verify a narrower permission design separately before removal.
permissions.review: Real current-tab selection flow; potentially redundant with persistent HTTP(S) access. The marketing workflow does not remove permissions.

permissions.justification: Adds Translate selection and Translate page commands using createMenus and chrome.contextMenus.onClicked in extension/src/background.ts. The selection command sends the chosen text to the content script; the page command starts the Pro workflow or opens the Pro purchase page for Free access. Browser context menu entries require this API permission.

Uses chrome.storage.local for language, theme, interface, selection, tone and page-context preferences, and chrome.storage.session for account/environment-scoped popup drafts, pending requests, page sessions and job ownership. These extension-wide settings and recoverable service-worker state cannot use an individual website’s storage. Completed translation history separately uses local IndexedDB, partitioned by account and environment, without cloud sync. Evidence: extension/src/background.ts settings/saveSettings/withSession, extension/src/shared/drafts.ts, and extension/src/shared/history.ts.

Reads selected text from accessible frames when the user opens the popup, and injects packaged content.js if an existing user-selected page lacks the content script. Evidence: extension/src/ui/main.tsx popup selection capture and extension/src/background.ts startPage fallback. chrome.scripting is needed for those dynamic operations; no remote executable code is fetched.

Uses chrome.identity.getAuthToken for Google sign-in and exchanges the credential for Firebase authentication. The verified account authorizes translation, tracks monthly character usage and connects subscription access. Sign-out clears cached tokens. Only openid, email and profile scopes are requested; Gmail, Drive, contacts and other account content are not requested. Evidence: extension/src/auth.ts login/logout/getIdToken and manifest.oauth2.scopes.

Enumerates documents and frames for user-started Pro page translation and handles their lifecycle. Navigation cancels jobs tied to old documents; eligible new frames join an active page session. History-state and fragment navigation end the old session. Evidence: extension/src/background.ts startPage/changePage getAllFrames and onCommitted/onDOMContentLoaded/onHistoryStateUpdated/onReferenceFragmentUpdated. activeTab does not provide these frame and navigation events. These events are used to manage active translation, not to compile browsing history.

Runs packaged content.js on ordinary HTTP webpages and accessible frames so the selected-text icon is ready on arbitrary sites. After user activation, Pro page translation reads eligible text, observes newly appearing text, replaces translations and restores originals. Optional context reads only eligible visible surrounding text. A fixed domain list would exclude arbitrary sites; activeTab alone would require manual activation before the current automatic selection-icon experience. Optional per-site permission would require a separate product-flow change. Evidence: manifest.content_scripts.matches/all_frames and extension/src/content/index.ts, dom.ts and context.ts.
permissions.review: Broad persistent site access should be justified explicitly. HTTP support is genuinely separate from HTTPS; do not claim the API itself requires HTTP.

permissions.justification: Provides the same selection icon, requested text translation and user-started Pro page translation on ordinary HTTPS sites and accessible frames. It also allows HTTPS requests to translation and authentication services. Backend-only host access would not support translating arbitrary websites; activeTab alone would not supply the pre-existing selection icon before a toolbar/menu action. Evidence: manifest.host_permissions/content_scripts, extension/src/content/index.ts/dom.ts/context.ts, extension/src/background.ts api, and extension/src/auth.ts. Chrome internal pages and the Web Store remain restricted.
permissions.review: The broad website requirement, rather than backend fetch alone, is the reason for this wildcard. Internal browser pages and the Chrome Web Store remain restricted.

oauthScopes.purpose: Authenticate the Google account used for translation access.
Identify the signed-in account and display its email in account settings.
Display the account name and profile information supplied through Google/Firebase.

publicationStatus: Chrome Web Store draft 1.3.1 verified on 2026-10-28: 55 descriptions and 275 localized screenshots saved, with icon, promotional graphics, privacy disclosures and testing instructions. Submit for review is available. Not submitted or published.
releaseChecks: Version 1.3.1 is uploaded and the Store draft fields are saved. All 55 descriptions and 275 localized screenshots were read back after reloading the saved draft; remote thumbnails passed image/order/locale checks. Review submission and publication remain separate actions.

55 message catalogs, listing descriptions and localized screenshot sets are included. The main translator UI remains English/Ukrainian; screenshot editorial text is localized around authentic English UI.
Localized text is drafted and structurally checked; independent native-language review is not claimed.
Broad website access remains required by the current automatic-selection and active Pro page-translation workflow. No new permissions were introduced for review or onboarding.
Google OAuth has no separate app username/password. Testing instructions explain Free testing and the support contact for complimentary Pro reviewer access; no shared Pro review account was supplied.

billing.annualAllowance: Monthly windows, not all annual characters at once

dataHandling.transfers: Requested text and opted-in page context go to the translation backend for server-side AI processing. Instant selection automatically sends selected text when enabled; an active page translation session processes eligible new text.
dataHandling.history: Local IndexedDB; separated by account/environment, no cloud sync, maximum 1,000 entries or 25 MiB. Free shows latest 20, Pro up to 1,000. Delete, clear and disable controls are supported.
dataHandling.pageContext: Pro opt-in; at most 2,000 visible surrounding characters; input fields, passwords, hidden text and HTML excluded.
